Wisk Aero and Archer Aviation, two of the most prominent eVTOL companies, announced Thursday that they've agreed to work together after settling a legal dispute\.

Both companies are working on electric aircraft which can takeoff and land vertically, but also have wings so they fly more like planes than helicopters\. They're commonly known as flying taxis, because they're designed for smaller distances\.

United Airlines has already ordered $1 billion worth of Archer's Midnight eVTOL, while Wisk is owned by Boeing, which has invested $450 million\.

As part of the companies' collaboration, Boeing has now also agreed to invest an undisclosed amount into Archer, as part of a $215 million funding round\.

And Wisk will now be Archer's exclusive provider of autonomous-flying technology\.

\"This strategic relationship will leverage each company's respective strengths and competencies with the goal of accelerating the commercialization of autonomous flight,\" Archer said in a press release\.

Archer added that the collaboration could potentially save it hundreds of millions of dollars\.

Wisk's eVTOL\. Wisk Aero

Wisk and Archer had been locked in a legal dispute since 2021, after the former accused the latter of stealing trade secrets\.

In court documents reviewed by Insider, Wisk accused its rival of \"a brazen theft of its intellectual property and confidential information\.\"

After Archer hired ten Wisk engineers, it produced an aircraft with \"a striking resemblance\" to a Wisk patent, the lawsuit alleges\.

Then Wisk hired an analyst for a forensic investigation which found two of those engineers downloaded thousands of files shortly before leaving for Archer, according to the lawsuit\.

But now, two years later, an undisclosed settlement has been reached while the two companies will quash the hostility and work together\.

Archer also announced Thursday that the Federal Administration Aviation has given approval for its Midnight aircraft to begin flight tests\.

It's aiming for FAA certification and commercial operations in 2025\.

Verocel’s unique expertise in the certification of high-integrity software advances Wisk’s autonomous certification effort

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif\.–BUSINESS WIRE–

Wisk Aero, a leading Advanced Air Mobility \(AAM\) company, announced today it has acquired Verocel Inc\., a software verification and validation \(V&V\) company\. Verocel’s unique expertise in supporting the certification of high-integrity aerospace software and the qualification of V&V tools will play a key role in Wisk’s ongoing effort to certify its Generation 6 autonomous, electric air taxi\.

This press release features multimedia\. View the full release here: https://www\.businesswire\.com/news/home/20240625141739/en/

Wisk Aero Acquires Verocel \(Graphic: Business Wire\)

For the past 25 years, the Verocel team has been leading the V&V of high-integrity software products within the aerospace industry\. The team has deep expertise in DO-178C and are members of industry standards committees for high-integrity software including RTCA/Special Committee, EUROCAE Working Group, and the FAA’s Overarching Properties Working Group\. Additionally, the qualified Verocel toolset – VeroTrace – provides a baseline for software certification requirements definition, tracking, and FAA submittals\. This specialty expertise creates an enduring capability at Wisk that supports both the certification of the Generation 6 aircraft as well as future software developments at The Boeing Company\.

“High-integrity software development is critical for our mission to certify an autonomous, electric aircraft with V&V being a significant portion of the total software certification effort,” said Brian Yutko, Wisk CEO\. “Verocel’s specialized and talented team will bring with them deep experience and rigor, helping to accelerate our autonomous certification project that is already well underway\. We are thrilled to have this talented team join Wisk\!”

Verocel was founded in 1999 and has a proven history with over 160 projects for 25\+ customers including previous work with The Boeing Company\. In addition to software development and V&V services, Verocel also develops and produces the safety computers for the Wide Area Augmentation System \(WAAS\), an air navigation system that enhances GPS accuracy and integrity to enable aircraft to safely navigate all over the world today\. Over 50 highly specialized software engineers, based in Westford Massachusetts and Poznan, Poland, join Wisk through this acquisition\.

“Wisk is a perfect alignment for Verocel, both in the long and short term,” said Jim Chelini, President of Verocel\. “Not only is this a chance to directly apply our expertise to the certification of a groundbreaking technology, but this is also an incredible opportunity for Verocel talent to excel within Wisk and the broader Boeing ecosystem long term\.”

Verocel will continue to deliver against customer commitments in addition to ramping up on the Wisk Generation 6 certification program\.

# Archer & Boeing Partner to Advance AI in Aviation - Newsy Today

Archer Aviation stock rose 12% on Monday to close at its highest level in over two months after the air-taxi company agreed to acquire three business units from Boeing, according to MarketWatch\. As part of the transaction, Boeing takes a 19\.75% stake in Archer and enters a technology-sharing arrangement focused on autonomous and self-flying aircraft\.

## Boeing Acquires 19\.75% Stake in Archer Aviation

Boeing is taking a 19\.75% equity stake in Archer Aviation under the newly announced agreement, according to MarketWatch\. The deal links the major aerospace manufacturer directly with the electric vertical take-off and landing \(eVTOL\) developer\. Alongside the equity investment, the two companies established a technology-sharing partnership dedicated to autonomous flight systems\.

Following the announcement, shares of Archer climbed 12% on Monday, closing out the session at their highest mark in more than two months, according to MarketWatch data\. Meanwhile, Boeing’s stock fell nearly 1% as the manufacturing giant continues a broader corporate turnaround\.

Did You Know?

The Federal Aviation Administration \(FAA\) launched a specific pilot program for electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft in March, with trial runs scheduled to span three years after the initial project becomes operational, according to the FAA\.

## Insitu, Wisk Aero, and SkyGrid Transferred to Archer

Boeing is shedding three specific business units as part of an ongoing effort to focus strictly on core jet-making operations, according to MarketWatch\. The units included in the sale are drone-maker Insitu, electric autonomous air-taxi developer Wisk Aero, and SkyGrid, which provides an air-traffic management system for autonomous flights\.

While financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed by either company, analysts at Jefferies noted that Insitu generates approximately $200 million in annual sales and operates profitably, according to MarketWatch reporting\. The broader transaction is expected to close by the end of the year\.

Boeing stated that the agreement “creates an end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense,” according to MarketWatch\. The company added that the move allows Wisk, SkyGrid, and Insitu “to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses\.”

## Gaining an Edge Over Competitors in the Air-Taxi Sector

The acquisition of Boeing’s three units grants Archer Aviation a distinct strategic advantage over rivals in the emerging eVTOL industry, including Joby Aviation, according to MarketWatch analysis\. By absorbing Wisk Aero and SkyGrid alongside drone-maker Insitu, Archer secures crucial infrastructure and autonomous flight technology\.

Boeing has spent recent months divesting ancillary divisions to streamline its operations around core commercial jet manufacturing\. By trading these units for a nearly 20% equity stake in Archer, Boeing maintains financial exposure to the advanced air mobility sector without directing internal operational bandwidth away from its primary manufacturing turnaround\.

# Boeing exits the air taxi business, sells Wisk, SkyGrid, and Insitu to Archer Aviation

ⓘ Archer AviationArcher Aviation Model M001 is a prototype eVTOL aircraft designed to carry a pilot and four passengers\.

Boeing is selling Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu to Archer Aviation while taking an equity stake in the eVTOL developer\. The deal strengthens Archer's air taxi ambitions and allows Boeing to refocus on its core commercial aircraft business\.

Boeing has agreed to sell three of its advanced aviation subsidiaries to Archer Aviation while taking a 19\.75% stake in the California-based electric air taxi developer\. According to a regulatory filing, Boeing will also receive options to purchase additional Class A shares over the next four years\. The deal includes autonomous aircraft developer Wisk Aero, urban air mobility software company SkyGrid, and drone manufacturer Insitu\.

The acquisition significantly expands Archer's technology portfolio as the company races to launch commercial air taxi services\. Boeing will retain access to Wisk's autonomous flight technology for its commercial and defense programs, while the two companies will also share technology\.

Wisk Aero was founded in 2019 as a joint venture between Boeing and Kitty Hawk, the flying taxi startup backed by Google co-founder Larry Page\. The company has developed six generations of autonomous eVTOL \(electric vertical takeoff and landing\) aircraft and completed more than 1,700 flight tests\.

The deal also includes SkyGrid, which develops air traffic management systems for future urban air mobility networks, and Insitu, a Boeing subsidiary that manufactures long-endurance unmanned aircraft used by the U\.S\. military\.

The transaction allows Boeing to sharpen its focus on its core commercial aircraft business as it works through an order backlog worth about $715 billion, representing more than 6,200 aircraft yet to be delivered\.

For Archer, the acquisition comes as it prepares to launch pilot air taxi services in New York, Texas, and Florida before the end of the year\. The company has also expanded into the defense sector, recently unveiling a military-focused eVTOL aircraft developed with Anduril Industries\.

Boeing said the transaction will allow the acquired businesses to accelerate product development while enabling the aerospace giant to continue benefiting from technologies it has invested in over the past two decades\. Archer CEO Adam Goldstein described the acquisition as \"a watershed moment\" that will help diversify the company's business and accelerate revenue growth\.

The deal also marks the latest chapter in the relationship between Archer and Wisk\. In 2021, Wisk sued Archer over alleged trade secret theft and patent infringement\. The dispute was settled in 2023, with Wisk agreeing to become Archer's exclusive provider of autonomous flight technology\.

# Former rivals unite as Archer acquires three Boeing aerospace subsidiaries

**Archer Aviation** has agreed to acquire **Boeing **subsidiaries **Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid** in a deal that reshapes one of the aerospace industry's most unusual rivalries while expanding Archer beyond the urban air mobility market\. Boeing will also become one of Archer's largest shareholders and collaborate with the company on future autonomous aviation technologies\.

The transaction combines businesses operating in different segments of advanced aerospace\. Archer is developing the **Midnight** electric air taxi for commercial passenger transport, while **Wisk** has spent more than a decade designing fully autonomous eVTOL aircraft\.

Insitu is an established manufacturer of military unmanned aircraft, including the ScanEagle family used for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions, and SkyGrid develops digital airspace management software intended to support the growing use of autonomous aircraft\.

Boeing said the partnership will allow it to continue accessing technologies developed by the three businesses while Archer gains engineering capabilities and products that extend well beyond the electric air taxi market\.

The announcement also marks a remarkable turnaround in the relationship between Archer and Wisk\.

In 2021, **Wisk filed a lawsuit accusing Archer** of misappropriating trade secrets after hiring former Wisk engineers\. The company alleged that confidential information had been used during the development of Archer's aircraft, while Archer denied the accusations and argued that it had developed its technology independently\.

Midnight eVTOL \(Archer Aviation \)

The legal dispute became one of the highest-profile cases in the emerging urban air mobility sector, which at the time was attracting billions of dollars in investment as dozens of startups competed to certify electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft\.

The conflict ended in 2023 when Boeing, Wisk and Archer reached a settlement\. Boeing invested in Archer, all litigation was dismissed and Wisk agreed to become the exclusive supplier of autonomous flight technology for future autonomous variants of Archer's aircraft\.

The acquisition also gives Archer an immediate foothold in the defense market through Insitu, whose unmanned aircraft are already in operational service with military customers worldwide\. Together with Wisk's autonomy expertise and SkyGrid's airspace management technology, the deal positions Archer as a broader aerospace company spanning commercial advanced air mobility, autonomous aviation and defense systems\.

# Archer agrees to acquire Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu from Boeing

The Boeing Company and Archer Aviation Inc\. today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries\.

The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing \(eVTOL\) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems \(UAS\) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense\.

Wisk, SkyGrid and Inset have pioneered and incubated core autonomous flight technologies for the future that, in combination with Archer’s air taxi, UAS and AI technologies, will bring new and innovative solutions to the market\.

These companies, with nearly two million combined flight hours, are expected to bring a deep autonomy foundation to Archer’s ZEE artificial intelligence platform\. This positions Archer to deliver an end-to-end physical AI platform across commercial aerospace, defense and air traffic management that can lead the next generation of aviation\.

Archer’s founder and CEO, Adam Goldstein, said: “This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense\. This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business\.”

In conjunction with the transaction, Boeing and Archer are entering into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement through which Boeing will retain access to the Wisk core autonomous flight technology for its current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft\.

The transaction allows Boeing to retain strategic upside through its stake in Archer and simultaneously focus current and future investments into Boeing’s core businesses\.

“This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development\.

“It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses\. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it’s clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market\. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy\.”

About the companies:

- Wisk is the only company that has designed, built and flown six generations of eVTOL aircraft, amassing 1,700-plus flight tests\. Over the past 16 years, Wisk’s world-class team has developed unmatched autonomy capabilities powered by a next-gen flight-control computer, sensor suite, and radar system designed for certification in both civil and potential defense markets\.
- SkyGrid has built a leading ground-based, aircraft-agnostic air traffic management solution that establishes the digital foundation for the future of automated airspace\. SkyGrid enables safe integration, scalable automation and coordinated traffic management that is necessary for commercialization across the aviation ecosystem\.
- Insitu is a pioneer in designing, developing and manufacturing uncrewed aircraft systems \(UAS\) used in intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance\. Its product portfolio spans high-performance, cost-effective, resilient, VTOL-capable UAS and AI-enabled software solutions\. Insitu’s technologies have helped the armed forces of 35 nations make quicker, more informed decisions to bring warfighters home safely\. With offices in the U\.S\., Australia, the U\.K\., and the UAE, Insitu has manufactured and fielded more than 3,500 UAS and provides operations and support networks in every hemisphere of the globe\.

Additional details of the transaction are available in Archer’s Form 8-K filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission\.

The transaction remains subject to certain agreed-upon closing conditions, including expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act and is expected to close by the end of 2026\.

# Who is Archer, the company buying three businesses from Boeing?

**Archer Aviation** drew attention on Monday after **Boeing **announced an **agreement to sell three of its subsidiaries** to the California-based company: autonomous eVTOL developer **Wisk Aero**, military drone manufacturer **Insitu **and airspace management software company **SkyGrid**\.

The transaction raises an obvious question: who is Archer, a company founded only eight years ago that is now taking control of businesses that have spent years or even decades under Boeing?

Archer is one of the best-funded survivors of the eVTOL boom that emerged around the beginning of the decade\. It was created in 2018 to develop electric aircraft for short urban trips and quickly attracted investors and large industrial partners\. Its main aircraft, Midnight, however, is still undergoing certification and has yet to enter regular commercial service\.

### Two tech entrepreneurs enter aviation

Archer was founded in California in October 2018 by **Adam Goldstein and Brett Adcock**\. Neither had a background in aircraft manufacturing\.

The two entrepreneurs had previously founded Vettery, an online recruitment platform that was acquired by Adecco\. They subsequently invested in Archer and recruited engineers from companies already working on electric aircraft, including Airbus' Vahana program and Wisk\.

Brett Adcock and Adam Goldstein \| **Archer**

The company's first major aircraft was Maker, a two-seat demonstrator unveiled in 2021\. It used 12 electric propellers mounted on a fixed wing and was intended primarily to validate the configuration Archer planned to use on its commercial aircraft\.

Maker completed its first hover flight in December 2021 and its first complete transition from vertical to wing-borne flight in November 2022\.

By then, **Archer had unveiled Midnight**\.

The larger aircraft accommodates one pilot and four passengers and is intended mainly for short flights of around 20 miles \(32 km\)\. Midnight first flew in October 2023 and completed its first full transition in June 2024\. Piloted flight testing followed\.

Archer Hero \| **Archer**

### United, Stellantis and ambitious promises

Archer's rise was unusually fast for an aircraft manufacturer\.

In 2021, United Airlines announced an agreement covering up to 200 aircraft and later paid Archer $10 million as a pre-delivery payment\. The companies even presented proposed air taxi routes linking Manhattan with Newark Airport and downtown Chicago with O'Hare\.

Archer also developed a close relationship with **Stellantis**\. What began as cooperation with Fiat Chrysler evolved into investment and industrial assistance, including the development of Archer's Midnight manufacturing operation in Georgia\.

That same year, Archer went public through a merger with SPAC Atlas Crest Investment Corp\.

Archer \| **Archer**

Its early forecasts were aggressive\. Archer expected to obtain FAA certification in 2024 and begin commercial operations shortly afterward\. It also contemplated producing hundreds of aircraft annually by the middle of the decade\.

Those targets were not met\.

As of August 2026, Midnight remains without an FAA type certificate and production is still far from the volumes projected five years ago\. The certification program has nevertheless advanced, and the FAA accepted all of Archer's proposed Means of Compliance earlier this year\.

The company is also preparing limited operations under government programs in the United States and the United Arab Emirates while certification continues\.

Wisk eVTOL \| **Wisk Aero**

### The company it once fought in court

One of the most unusual chapters in Archer's short history involves Wisk, one of the three Boeing businesses it is now acquiring\.

Wisk sued Archer in April 2021, accusing its new competitor of trade secret misappropriation and patent infringement\. Several employees hired by Archer had previously worked for Wisk\.

Archer denied the allegations and said its aircraft had been independently developed\. A federal judge declined to issue the preliminary injunction sought by Wisk, and the litigation continued until August 2023, when **Archer, Wisk and Boeing reached a settlement**\.

The settlement produced an unexpected relationship\. Wisk and Archer agreed to cooperate on autonomous flight technology, and Boeing invested in Archer\.

There was also a change at the top of the company\. Adcock left the co-CEO position in 2022 and later departed Archer altogether\. Goldstein became sole CEO and remains in charge today\.

Insitu drone \| **Insitu**

### From electric air taxis to defense

Under Goldstein, Archer began moving into businesses beyond the Midnight program\.

In 2025 and 2026, the company acquired technology and assets associated with other advanced air mobility developers, including Lilium and Overair, and expanded its facilities in California\.

It also entered the defense sector through work with Anduril\. At the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026, the companies unveiled a hybrid VTOL platform being developed as Thunder for military applications and Halo for commercial missions\.

Unlike the battery-electric Midnight, the new aircraft uses hybrid propulsion and is being developed for autonomous operations\.

**Archer** has simultaneously moved into artificial intelligence with ZEE, a system intended to combine aircraft information with ADS-B traffic, weather, terrain, aeronautical charts and air traffic control communications\.

The result is a company that increasingly bears little resemblance to the electric air taxi startup created in 2018\.

Wisk eVTOL \| **Wisk Aero**

### And now, three Boeing businesses

The agreement announced on August 10 accelerates that transformation\.

Archer will acquire Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid\. Wisk adds more than a decade of autonomous eVTOL development\. SkyGrid develops software for autonomous aviation and airspace management\.

Insitu brings something substantially different: an established defense operation\.

Founded in 1994 and acquired by Boeing in 2008, Insitu developed unmanned aircraft including ScanEagle and Integrator\. More than 3,500 of its aircraft have been produced, and Boeing and Archer say the business generates more than $200 million in annual revenue\.

Boeing will receive shares corresponding to approximately 19\.75% of Archer's Class A stock before closing, subject to adjustments, as well as warrants linked to another potential $200 million investment\. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026\.

Wisk eVTOL \| **Wisk Aero**

Archer has the financial resources to continue expanding\. It ended June with approximately $1\.56 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, although its business remains heavily loss-making\. The company posted a $263\.2 million net loss in the second quarter of 2026\.

The Boeing agreement therefore brings together two very different sides of Archer\.

**Follow Air Data News:** **WhatsApp** \| **Instagram** \| **LinkedIn** \| **Twitter** \| **Facebook**

The company still has not achieved the objective for which it was founded: certifying an electric aircraft and putting it into regular passenger service\. But in eight years it has gone from an unknown startup created by two technology entrepreneurs to a publicly traded aerospace company backed by United, Stellantis and Boeing, with activities increasingly extending into defense, autonomous aircraft and aviation software\.

And perhaps nothing illustrates that transformation better than Wisk\. In 2021, the Boeing-backed company was trying to stop Archer in federal court\. In 2023, the two became technology partners\. In 2026, Archer is preparing to become its owner\.
